date-fns:split:fp.why: Rank 0 buries 382 of 398 curried wrappers so 16 stay at the top; rank 1 moves 397 of 398. Both are the same non-statement about a flat generated namespace.

date-fns:split:locale.why: Rank 1 is the corpus's most interesting rejection: en-AU/en-CA/en-GB/en-IE/en-IN/en-NZ/en-US/en-ZA is a genuinely nameable group (`en`), and the cut is still wrong -- date-fns/locale/en-US is a published entry point, so grouping them is a breaking API change. Nameable is necessary, not sufficient.

date-fns:split:parse/_lib.why: Separates constants/parsers/utils from Parser/Setter/types, which is close to abstract-versus-concrete and would leave the already-existing parsers/ directory nested one level deeper for no gain.

date-fns:split:parse/_lib/parsers.why: Both candidates are arbitrary halves of 32 sibling parser classes, which are exactly the parallel instances that should stay flat.

flask:split:.why: Both candidates are arbitrary halves of a flat package. app/blueprints/cli/config/helpers/json/signals/testing/wrappers shares no idea; neither does the remainder.

requests:split:.why: Rank 0 splits the package down the middle with no idea on either side; rank 1 evicts __version__ and help, which is a two-file eviction wearing a subdirectory's clothes.

rich:split:.name: live
rich:split:.why: The one accepted proposal in the corpus. live/progress/spinner/status/_spinners/filesize is a real cluster -- progress imports live, spinner and filesize; status imports live and spinner; spinner imports _spinners -- and `live` names it. Ranks 0 and 2 are arbitrary halves of a 78-file flat package.

tanstack-router:costs:router-core/src/ss.label: taxonomy
tanstack-router:costs:router-core/src/ss.why: RawStream, ShallowErrorPlugin, seroval-plugins, transformer: one connected component implementing SSR payload serialization. Small and cohesive, not a bag. The bit cost dislikes it only because it is small and externally addressed.

tanstack-router:split:react-router/src.why: Rank 0 moves 20 .tsx files and leaves 15 more behind, so it is not a components/non-components separation; the nearest honest name is `components`, which names a file shape rather than an idea. Rank 1 mixes the use* hooks with route/router/link.

vite:costs:node/__tests__/fixtures.label: convention
vite:costs:node/__tests__/fixtures.why: Test fixtures. Their layout is dictated by what the test harness loads, not by the dependency graph; this subtree should have been --excluded.

vite:costs:node/__tests__/fixtures/runne.label: convention
vite:costs:node/__tests__/fixtures/runne.why: Test fixtures. Their layout is dictated by what the test harness loads, not by the dependency graph; this subtree should have been --excluded.

vite:costs:shared.label: junk_drawer
vite:costs:shared.why: Four components in a directory named `shared`, reached from eight different directories. builtin/constants/utils have nothing to do with hmr/ssrTransform; the only cross-child link is three files touching moduleRunnerTransport.

vite:split:.why: module-runner/node/types against client/shared -- five top-level directories are already the repo's structure, and neither half is a concept.

vite:split:node.why: The proposal PR 4c built the spectral search to reach, and it does not survive reading: rank 1's group is cli, logger, shortcuts, preview, watch, http, env, publicDir, external, nodeResolve, idResolver, assetSource, deprecations, typeUtils -- a grab bag. Rank 0 is the complement and no better. 373 bits of evidence for a cut with no name.

vite:split:node/__tests__.why: Moves fixtures/ and runnerImport.spec.ts out of a test directory. Test layout is not the graph's business.

vite:split:shared.why: Consistent with the costs verdict on the same directory: the right advice for a junk drawer is dissolve it, not subdivide it. Rank 0 also splits hmr.ts from hmrHandler.ts.

zod:costs:v3/helpers.label: junk_drawer
zod:costs:v3/helpers.why: enumUtil, errorUtil, parseUtil, partialUtil, typeAliases, util -- five components, no shared target, and every member is named after being a utility rather than after doing anything.

zod:costs:v4/locales.label: taxonomy
zod:costs:v4/locales.why: 52 per-language error-message tables, all 52 importing v4/core/errors.ts and 50 of them core/checks.ts and core/util.ts. Parallel instances of one category; dissolving them into v4/ would be absurd.

zod:split:.why: Moving mini/, v3/ and v4/ into a box beside index.ts and v4-mini/ adds a level without adding a concept.

zod:split:v3.why: Rank 1 nearly finds the error subsystem (ZodError, errors, locales) and then puts benchmarks/ in with it, which is the difference between a module and a cut.

zod:split:v4.why: The corpus's largest split by bits (-652) and a non-finding: rank 0 moves everything except the barrel down one level, which is v4/src/, not a module. Rank 1 pairs classic/ with index.ts for no reason a reader would recognise.

zod:split:v4/classic.why: coerce/compat/errors/external/parse/schemas against checks/from-json-schema/index/iso/tests -- no idea on either side, and 1.8 bits of evidence for it.

zod:split:v4/mini.why: Moves index.ts and tests/ into a box. Neither is a module.
